articles.title: Palmer Luckey’s Anduril is getting into laptops — and claims they’ll be American-made
articles.summary: Anduril and Qualcomm are working together on a new laptop line called BlueChip, assembled in the US. Their lofty goal is to one day fully make them in America.
articles.body: Anduril and Qualcomm are partnering on a new line of laptops called BlueChip, launching in early 2027. The first prototype is a ruggedized model using Arm-based Snapdragon X series chips and aimed at the US military, but the ultimate focus of the joint venture is to make laptops entirely in the US. Eventually. The global supply chain of computers and laptops normally involves China, Taiwan, and many other countries, so the first BlueChip laptops will only be “designed and assembled in the United States,” per Anduril’s official press release. Assembly is planned to be done at Anduril’s Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio. Anduril and Qualcomm aren’t sharing many details on how they’re going to build enough manufacturing in the US for a laptop that’s 100-percent domestically made. During a virtual Q&A session with media that included The Verge, Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon laid out the motivations for American-made (or at least, American-assembled) laptops. It’s the talking points you’d expect: keeping US money in the US, the potential for creating domestic jobs, minimizing technological / economic reliance on other countries, and reducing national security vulnerabilities. [Image: [Image: When asked what percentage of the BlueChip laptop’s components will be made in the US once it launches in 2027, Luckey said, “TBD. . . Those questions are not settled.” The components Luckey specified that are planned to be American-made from the start are the display glass, the frame around the display, and parts of the ribbon component. “I think most likely the thing that we ship is not going to be 100-percent American.” It sounds like BlueChip’s first laptop will be well below the 65-percent requirement to count as American-made under federal procurement rules.s A promo image provided by Anduril shows hardware stamped with “Built in America.” As for the chips in BlueChip, Qualcomm’s Amon told The Verge it intends to manufacture processors for this laptop at TSMC Arizona. When The Verge followed up to ask how much money Qualcomm is investing into that, Qualcomm communications rep Yelena Tebcherani said, “We don’t have any more details to share at the moment.” Anduril’s first potential customer for BlueChip laptops is the same as its drones: the US military. The prototype is a ruggedized computer aimed at military personnel, complete with a rifle strap-style carrying handle — presumably so a soldier can slam the laptop shut, quickly grab it, and get on the move. It will run Windows or two undisclosed versions of Linux. [Image: The BlueChip laptop’s tan, rugged exterior. During the Q&A, Luckey indicated that BlueChip is funded entirely by Anduril and Qualcomm, not government subsidies. He mentioned that Anduril is starting with a military laptop to first service users with the most stringent hardware needs and software security demands. It’s also likely for pursuing those valuable government contracts that could call for large quantities of expensive computers. After the government and defense sectors, Anduril’s next target will be first responders and public safety, before eventually getting to consumer-level laptops — the lowest on the priority list. Luckey mentioned offhandedly, “I’d say the worst case here is that this is going to be a low volume laptop for critical industries and government needs that desperately need something like this to exist.” Palmer Luckey is of course a controversial figure, with his history of fueling right wing troll farms motivated by his political beliefs. Anduril is better known for making drones and autonomous weapons, while Luckey continues making consumer-facing products like Game Boy clones — often polarizing the communities they’re meant to serve. Bringing a supply chain for computers back to the US and one day manufacturing a fully American-made laptop sounds a tall order. It’s complicated even further once you consider the person and company behind it.

articles.title: Apple updates the MacBook Pro with M6 chips
articles.summary: The entry-level MacBook Pro gets Apple’s latest silicon including its N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
articles.body: Apple is giving its entry-level MacBook Pro a spec bump. After upgrading the entry-level MacBook Pro with its M5 chip a year ago, Apple is refreshing the laptop today with the M6 chip, which the company launched in August as part of recent upgrades to the new Mac Mini. Last year’s entry-level MacBook Pro update brought minimal changes from the M4 model that debuted a year prior, including the same design, port layout, webcam, and speakers. The most notable updates, aside from the then-new M5 processor, was faster storage and the option to upgrade its capacity to a hefty 4TB for an extra $1,200. [Image: Ports on the new M6 version of the 14-inch MacBook Pro include HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, an SDXC card slot, and a 3.5mm headphone jack. It’s a similar story for 2026. Announced this morning through a press release, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro features three Thunder 4 USB-C ports that all support charging and DisplayPort connectivity, a MagSafe 3 charging port, full-size HDMI, and an SDXC memory card slot accommodating photographers. It carries forward the same 12MP Center Stage camera and Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, but this year the 14-inch MacBook Pro is getting an upgrade to both Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 through the Apple N1 wireless networking chip that was previously only included on MacBook Pro configurations with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. [Image: Apple says the M6 chip in the MacBook Pro delivers up to “30 percent faster graphics performance” compared to its M5 chip thanks to a 12-core GPU. Pricing for the new M6 version of the 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 with 16GB of memory, the same as last year’s M5 model. Bumping that to 24GB increases the price to $2,199, while 32GB is $2,399. Included storage starts at 1TB, but increasing that is now more expensive as a result of the current memory shortage. Bumping that to 2TB is an extra $500, while 4TB is now an extra $1,500. Preorders start on October 28th and shipping is expected to begin on November 6th. The new M6 processor is Apple’s first 2nm chip with a bump to a 12-core CPU, up from 10 cores in the M5, and the company says it offers up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance when compared to its predecessor. The M6 also features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine to handle heavy on-device AI tasks, plus an upgraded 12-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in each core. In addition to performance improvements, Apple says its M6 processor is more power efficient.

articles.title: Apple refreshes the iMac with M6 chips
articles.summary: The latest iMac generation has the same M6 chipset that Apple launched with the Mac Mini in August.
articles.body: Apple is updating the iMac with M6 chips. The new iMac generation was introduced today, giving Apple’s all-in-one desktop computer a performance boost via the same chipset Apple launched with the Mac Mini in August. Prices start from $1,499, and the design otherwise appears largely unchanged. The update was announced ahead of Apple’s “Pro and Tell” event that’s scheduled to take place on Wednesday. This refresh comes two years after Apple gave the iMac an overhaul with M4 chips, meaning we’re skipping the M5 series entirely on this hardware. That should make this upgrade more meaningful. The M6 is Apple’s first 2nm chip and includes a dual 16-core Neural Engine that can boost performance when running on-device AI tasks. According to Apple’s press release, the M6-powered iMac “delivers up to 5x faster on-device AI performance” compared to the M4 model. The M6 configurations start from a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU for $1,499, which is the same price as the 8-core CPU-equipped M4 iMac. There’s also a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU starting at $1,699. Preorders will launch at 1:10PM ET on October 28th, and it’ll be fully available starting November 6th. Besides the chip upgrade, the new iMac isn’t getting much in the way of a hardware refresh. It now has Apple’s N1 wireless networking chip, alongside Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 on the base model instead of just the higher-spec variant. It still carries over the same Thunderbolt limitations as the M4 iMac, however — you only get two ports on the 10-core version, and four on the 12-core upgrade. There are also some new restrictions and fees included in the configuration options. If you want to customize the iMac with a Magic Trackpad instead of a Magic Mouse, it’ll cost you an extra $50, despite this being a free switch on the previous iMac. Ethernet has been upgraded from 1 gigabit to 2.5 gigabit, but thats now a $30 premium upgrade compared to sticking with a Wi-Fi only configuration. Apple also won’t let you configure the M6 iMac with a Magic Keyboard that has Touch ID but not a numeric keypad — despite showing an image of that on the new iMac announcement page. [Image: Why show me a non-numpad option keyboard if I can’t actually configure this with it Apple? If you were hoping for some new color options then, hard luck. Apple is offering the exact same color variants as it did with the M4, to the point where it’s just reused some of the marketing imagery and updated them to display more up-to-date content. The M6 chip provides a nice performance boost, but otherwise this is a small spec bump for Apple’s colorful all-in-one.

articles.title: We’ve had touchscreen laptops for years. Can Apple make them better?
articles.summary: Apple is poised to reverse course on a feature its executives openly mocked.
articles.body: A fridge is about to be merged with a toaster. Dogs and cats are soon to be living together. But it’s not mass hysteria; Apple is expected to finally announce a touchscreen MacBook tomorrow at its “Pro and Tell” event. A laptop with a touchscreen should be no big deal — we’ve had them for ages. But Apple took a hardline stance against them. In addition to Tim Cook’s infamous 2012 quote equating it to combining kitchen appliances, Steve Jobs emphatically dismissed touchscreen laptops as “ergonomically terrible” back in 2010, saying, “Touch surfaces don’t want to be vertical.” The closest Apple got was the MacBook Pro Touch Bar, from 2016 to 2023, but that horizontal landing strip for your fingers on the keyboard deck mostly amounted to unrealized potential. It sacrificed physical function keys (and for a while, the escape key) in favor of a non-deterministic UI. A touchscreen on a laptop is an established idea we already know can be useful for taking direct action on things around your screen — whether with an occasional tap and flick or through prolonged stylus use. So how is Apple going to do it exactly? How will the company that puts the word “magic” in some of its product names bring the magic to a touchscreen MacBook? For starters, rumors indicate this touch-enabled MacBook Pro will have a new OLED display. That sounds great, because OLEDs are awesome for deep blacks and vivid color contrast, though it’s likely to make them even more expensive. They’re rumored to use the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips and come in 14- and 16-inch sizes like their contemporaries. In our current RAMageddon world, the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro currently starts at $2,499. Now add a pricier OLED touch panel to it. Woof. [Image: The ill-fated Touch Bar is the only bit of touchscreen we’ve gotten on a MacBook thus far. The screen is also speculated to have a Dynamic Island cutout for the webcam instead of a notch. While I don’t love the notch, I’m firmly in the “It’s fine — you stop noticing it when you use it for a while” camp. The Dynamic Island should be a small aesthetic improvement, and if it operates as it does on iPhones, then it could also offer some touch-based multitasking with timers and music apps tucking info into it. The touchscreen MacBook is also rumored to have a thinner and lighter chassis design. The MacBook Pros got thicker and heavier with the M1 Pro / M1 Max generation after years of chasing thinness — that pursuit brought us worse thermals and the dreaded butterfly keyboards. Frankly, this rumor makes me the most nervous, because I don’t want a MacBook Pro that once again risks performance compromises for the sake of thinness. Not now, not ever again. Can Apple make its high-end MacBooks thinner again without compromising raw performance, battery, or quality of life? And what will the new MacBook’s touchscreen setup be like? How will you interact with it? Will it remain a conventional clamshell design, or will Apple give its hinge any added flexibility to allow new ways to use it via touch? I recently wrote about how fun I find 2-in-1 convertible laptops like Lenovo’s Yoga line, which has a hinge that folds all the way around and includes a stylus for mounting to the chassis. It’d be great to see Apple showcase something boldly exciting as it “pros and tells,” but I won’t be surprised if the first touchscreen MacBook keeps things safe with a standard clamshell. [Image: I don’t mind the slight chunkiness of current MacBook Pros, but lightening their load could be nice. Whether it’s a clamshell or a convertible, will this MacBook work with an Apple Pencil, or will it be touch-only? I hope Apple Pencil support is included, along with magnetic charging like on iPads, since it seems like a no-brainer for designers to use a precision tool for drawing on a touch-friendly Mac. But even if it works with an Apple Pencil, this will still be a Mac through and through — not an iPad. Apple is expected to introduce a revised macOS 27 Golden Gate with touch-friendly enhancements just for this new MacBook, while keeping it a full-blown desktop OS. Since this MacBook is unlikely to replace current models in Apple’s lineup (the MacBook Pros with Pro and Max-level chips were just updated earlier this year), this is likely to be an offshoot of macOS. MacBook Pros have mostly been about chip bumps and modest feature improvements since the M1 Pro and M1 Max generation revitalized the line in 2021. An OLED touchscreen model represents a major shakeup, and like the iPhone Duo there’s room for messiness or weird new quirks due to Apple design decisions. We’ll learn tomorrow what Apple deems is the “right” way for a touchscreen to work on a Mac.

articles.title: Apple unveils new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new MacBook Pro comes with 24 hours of battery life, and now features support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity.
articles.body:
Apple on Tuesday unveiled its new 14-inch MacBook Pro, powered by its latest M6 chip. The new MacBook Pro has 24 hours of battery life and now supports for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity. The laptop starts at $1,999 and is available in space black and silver.

Apple also announced its latest iMac , which is also powered by the M6 chip. The tech giant revealed the new devices just a day before its “Pro and Tell” event scheduled for Wednesday. On Monday, Apple announced its new iPad mini .

The tech giant says the M6 chip features a 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core and a 12-core GPU that delivers more responsive performance, up to 30% faster graphics, and up to 25% faster AI workloads compared with the M5 chip.

The M6 delivers up to 13 times the LLM prompt-processing speed of the M1 MacBook Pro and up to 1.3 times faster performance than the M5 model, Apple says.

The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, and has memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s, up from the 153GB/s on the M5 chip.

It includes HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack. Like previous models, the laptop features a 12-megapixel camera.

The M6 MacBook Pro supports fast charging, reaching up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with a compatible high-wattage USB-C power adapter.

As for the new M6-powered iMac, it features a faster CPU and GPU, with Neural Accelerators built into every core. Apple says the M6 delivers smooth multitasking and powerful performance for everyday apps, photo editing, and video production.

The new iMac starts at $1,499 and comes in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver.

The company also notes that the new iMac delivers up to five times faster on-device AI performance than the M4 model. It features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, an advanced camera and audio system, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports, color-matched accessories, and macOS 27.

Both the new MacBook Pro and iMac can be preordered starting October 28 and will be available starting November 6.

articles.body: Thanksgiving is less than a month away, so now’s a good time to start preparing before the rush. [Product: Apple AirTag (second-gen) | If you own an iPhone, the second-gen AirTag is the best Bluetooth tracker you can buy. That’s largely due to Apple’s ultra-wideband chip, which enables Precision Finding and guides you to an object’s exact location with on-screen arrows, vibrations, and sounds. The second-gen model can also help you find things faster than the prior generation, as it lets you pick up those directional cues from up to 50 percent farther (it also offers greater Bluetooth range). In our tests, that meant faster connections and better performance across multiple floors, which could come in handy if you’ve left something behind in a hotel. You can even follow directions on an Apple Watch Series 9 or later, making it possible to track down your stuff without pulling out your phone. The latest AirTag offers a few other perks for travelers, too. You can share it with up to five other people, which is handy if you’re traveling with family members. If your suitcase goes missing, you can also temporarily share its location with participating airlines, including both United and Delta. That means if your suitcase gets lost, airline staff can see its reported location, which can make it easier to track down and return to you. articles.title: My favorite robot vacuum just got quieter, and more expensive
articles.summary:
The new Matic Serene claims to be as quiet as your refrigerator while cleaning your floors. But it will cost you $1,700.
﻿
articles.body: Matic, the company behind my favorite robot vacuum, is launching its first new model since its 2023 debut: the Matic Serene. The new robotic floor cleaner has one key upgrade: noise reduction. With a promised output of just 52 decibels at its highest suction level, the Serene claims to be about as quiet as a running refrigerator. It costs $1,695, $200 more than the original Matic’s current price, and is available now. The good news is the company is offering an upgrade path for existing Matic owners. The Serene targets people “who are extremely noise sensitive,” cofounder and president Mehul Nariyawala tells The Verge. But beyond noise levels, it’s “exactly the same Matic.” The upgrade comes via a new hardware stack, and existing Matic owners can request a Serene hardware upgrade for their current model in early 2027. Loud robot vacuums often get shut off by annoyed owners, meaning they don’t finish their job and frustrate owners even more. (This happens a lot in my household.) That is why many bots have the option of a quiet mode, but these modes generally mean lower suction and less effective cleaning. The Matic Serene will clean on max power at just 52 decibels. “It’s very quiet on carpets, on hard surfaces; you mostly hear brush roll now,” says Nariyawala. The original Matic, which costs $1,495 and will continue to be sold, operates at 55 decibels. [Image: The Matic is taller than most robot vacuums — instead of using a large dock, it carries its dust bag and water tank with it. Matic takes a new approach to robot vacuums, with a form factor and navigation system different from most lidar-based disc robots sold by brands like iRobot, Roborock, Dreame, and others. Nariyawala told me that when the company developed Matic, they designed it to address the “seven deadly sins of robot vacuums,” with noise high on that list, along with getting stuck and dying under the couch. Many of today’s robot vacuums have a quiet mode that runs around 55 to 60 decibels, but they achieve this reduction by lowering suction power. In high-power mode, most are closer to 70 decibels. Matic launched with a claim of 55 decibels on its highest level and is now dropping by 3 more decibels, which could be a big deal for people who like to run their vacuums while at home. I’ve found I can use the Matic while working from home, but I sometimes need to shut it off if I am on a phone call. At 3 decibels quieter, I might not need to interrupt its work. [Product: Matic Serene | Existing owners can upgrade their Matic for the difference between their original purchase price and Serene’s price of $1,695. Matic has seen several price increases since it launched. The current model costs $1,495. However, someone may have purchased it for $1,095 when it first launched, meaning the upgrade could cost $600. That’s probably a tough sell. But if you gave up on robot vacuums because of noise, the Serene could be the solution you’ve been waiting for. I’ll be testing it soon and will have a full review.

articles.title: The Super Mouse puts a touchscreen macro pad under your hand
articles.summary: The $199 Super Mouse puts shortcuts, app launchers, timers, your schedule, and even a tiny keyboard on its 3-inch touchscreen.
articles.body: A company called Arctic Fox Technologies has announced a new multifunction mouse that forgoes a myriad of customizable shortcut buttons peppered across its surface for a compact touchscreen sitting beneath your hand. The Super Mouse may not prioritize ergonomics with its boxy design, but it can replace other peripherals on your desk, like a trackpad, macro pad, or streaming controller. If you’re faster at typing on your phone, the Super Mouse could potentially even replace a full-size keyboard with a smartphone-sized alternative that even includes swipe typing. The Super Mouse is now available for preorder through a Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign in which it’s discounted to $199 for backers, while full retail pricing will be $249. Delivery is expected to start in February 2027, but take that estimate with a grain of salt, as many Kickstarter campaigns have faced unforeseen delays. That price makes the Super Mouse more expensive than other companies’ attempts to merge mice and touchscreens. But while alternatives like Turtle Beach’s Command Series MC7 has just a 2.25-inch narrow display on the side, the Super Mouse features a 3.1-inch, 720 x 720 touchscreen positioned front and center beneath a pair of standard mouse buttons, a scroll wheel, and two customizable “hyper keys.” [Image: The Super Mouse doesn’t include a rechargeable battery and draws all the power it needs from a USB-C port, so using it wirelessly isn’t an option. That touchscreen will be most useful as a way to quickly launch apps through what its creators call a “Control Panel” that can include up to 16 shortcuts, macros, or launchers. The display’s functionality will change contextually and will present relevant shortcuts based on what app you’re using. If you’re working with video in Adobe Premiere, for example, the touchscreen will include editing and playback shortcuts. But if you have a specific workflow need, or the app you’re using isn’t recognized, the Super Mouse’s functionality can be customized using the company’s Flow desktop app. [Image: The Super Mouse will present app-specific controls such as playback and editing shortcuts for Adobe Premiere. Other touchscreen features include event and meeting reminders when synced with Google Calendar, voice-to-text capabilities processed locally on the mouse itself, multiple user profiles, focus timers, and productivity tracking. The mouse also includes a gyroscope so you can control slideshows or scrub video by just moving it around. The only feature seemingly missing is the ability to go wireless. Instead of a rechargeable battery, the Super Mouse draws all the power it needs from a USB-C port, so you’ll always need to keep it tethered to your PC.

articles.title: My divorce made headlines. Now I help survivors of toxic relationships tell their stories.
articles.summary: Elizabeth Chambers on rebuilding after her high-profile divorce from Armie Hammer, raising her kids and what survivors have taught her through her ID series...
articles.body:
When Elizabeth Chambers's marriage to actor Armie Hammer ended, she focused on a question many parents face: How do you rebuild your life while helping your children navigate theirs? Of course, not many have to do that with the world watching.

The journalist and entrepreneur announced her separation from Hammer in July 2020 after 10 years of marriage. The exes — who share daughter Harper, 12, and son Ford, 9 — spent years finalizing their divorce as the Call Me By Your Name actor faced public scandal and allegations of abuse. (Hammer has denied any nonconsensual sexual activity but acknowledged infidelity during their marriage.)

Chambers found a way to channel her pain into purpose. As host and executive producer of the Investigation Discovery (ID) series Toxic — which returns with tonight's two-hour special, Toxic: What Happened in the Haight House? — she explores cases of domestic abuse and intimate partner violence, helping survivors tell their stories and viewers recognize warning signs in their own relationships.

Here, Chambers reflects on starting over, what she's learned from survivors and how those lessons shape the way she raises her children, as told to Yahoo's Taryn Ryder.

When my marriage fell apart, I was trying to figure out how to move forward amid constant headlines about my personal life. I'd wake up thinking it might be an OK day, and hours later, it would all feel overwhelming. Sometimes, I turned off my phone for days. I leaned on trusted friends to tell me what I needed to know, and I just locked in with my kids.

During that time, I was compensating so much and trying to be so present and so fun and not let them see I was sad.

Starting over was a lot of therapy and a lot of woo-woo. Thankfully, it was during COVID, and I was on an island, which made it easier. There was a lot of writing things down (and burning it), sound baths and talking to people who had been through divorce.

In marriage, you both make vows, but you can't control anyone else's behavior or actions. Words are just words.

When everything falls apart, all you care about is protecting your kids. But that meant I had to do the work on myself, so I could be there for my children and not be an absolute mess.

I became deeply consumed by and obsessed with how to mitigate trauma in children. I talked to as many family separation therapists as I could find. In that work, what I realized is that family patterns — generational patterns — exist for a reason. That was just reinforced in Season 1 of Toxic .

From the time I was 3, I've known storytelling was my passion. I studied journalism at the University of Texas at Austin and graduated early for a job at Channel One. At Current TV, I learned rogue journalism: Check out a camera and go do a story. I found what I wanted to do: tell people's stories and connect with them.

Toxic is my dream job, and Season 1 solidified that. Immersing ourselves in survivors' lives and getting to know who they are at their core was so powerful. I still talk to all of them.

For Season 2, I wanted to level up in every way. We brought on a new showrunner I'd respected for a long time. We have two male survivors this season, and we cover more themes. Abuse comes in so many forms, and every episode is another example of that.

This isn't for headlines or clickbait. It's an opportunity to have your story told from beginning to end. With abuse comes shame. So often people want to shut down and they don't want to talk about it.

We don't come in, sit in a chair and leave. We get to know their friends and families. Sometimes we sit down for 10 or 12 hours. Our entire crew is deeply invested in hearing these stories and telling them respectfully. That's how we earn their trust, but it's not always easy. They don't know how it's going to turn out.

Nothing makes me happier than hearing someone say, "I knew it was going to be good because I felt safe, but I didn't know it was going to be this good."

"Just leave" never works, because that's what's so complicated with love.

When you have these complex feelings and when you have that deep connection with someone, your mind and your gut and your heart do not always work together. You don't want to hear it from the outside.

Try telling any of your friends who are so in love and have been dating someone for less than three months that it's not good. Some of us have been on both sides of it.

You have to give them an example, and that's why Toxic is so powerful. You can't say, "He's controlling you. He's depending on you. He's using your credit card to buy a motorcycle and a watch." You say, "Watch Episode 3 and see how this can end up."

Without a concrete example, people will say, "Oh, you're jealous," or, "Mind your own business." These are real cautionary tales that can be presented.

Raising children with boundaries and respect

This work literally informs everything I do.

I'm raising a daughter with very strong boundaries and a son who respects the heck out of women. I can say that without a single shadow of a doubt. It's almost like this is their life's work too, because they're surrounded by these conversations all the time. (Obviously, in an age-appropriate way.)

Those conversations can happen at any age. My daughter will be the first to read an unfair dynamic.

We'll watch TV shows that she likes, and we have conversations about what we see. Why are they doing it like this? It's never too young to have those conversations when it's framed the right way. You don't have to say it's about marriage or relationships. "Do you think that's balanced? Do you think they both have an equal voice? Do you think he respects her and she respects him? What do you think they're good at as a married couple?"

We have to raise good men and women. It's imperative, or we're going to keep having the headlines that we have right now.

I hope viewers recognize what they deserve and what they should expect, what is healthy and what's going to perpetuate good for their future generations.

If we're not going to do something for ourselves, do it for your kids. I've never been healthier than when I was pregnant. I love sugar. I eat BIRD Bakery [the bakery chain she founded] all the time. But when I was pregnant, I was so purposeful.

We do things for our kids that we won't do for ourselves. If you're in an abusive relationship or if you're in a toxic dynamic, if you're not going to do it for you, do it for your children.

My faith is really strong. When things seem the lowest and the darkest, you have to know that there is a reason you're going through that. The only way to get through it is to keep on going. It's not going to go away. You've got to just work through it.

If I could go back and tell myself something six years ago, I'd say, "You're going to turn lemons into lemonade. You really are. It's going to be better than OK." I wanted to do everything I could just to make sure that my kids were going to be better than OK. And we are.

Toxic: What Happened in the Haight House? premieres Oct. 27 at 9 p.m. ET/PT on ID and will be available to stream on HBO Max.

For anyone affected by abuse and needing support, call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233, or if you're unable to speak safely, you can log on to thehotline.org or text LOVEIS to 22522.

This account has been edited and condensed for length and clarity.

articles.title: 'Dancing with the Stars' Horror Movie Night ends in 2 eliminations, near walk-off
articles.summary: "Dancing with the Stars" Horror Movie Night saw Tyler Cameron's near-walk off, Shirley Ballas' tough critique and Val's return. See who was sent home.
articles.body:
Things got extra spooky on "Dancing with the Stars" as the show entered Week 7.

As Halloween creeps up, the 10 remaining couples took on Horror Movie Night on Tuesday, Oct. 27, with performances inspired by legendary horror films. To make things even scarier, eliminations resumed − and two couples were sent home − after nobody was eliminated during Dedication Night the week prior .

With just four shows remaining before the big finale, pressure was certainly be haunting the ballroom, and Shirley Ballas being the guest judge only raised the stakes more. She currently serves as head judge on the U.K.'s "Strictly Come Dancing" and appeared as a judge on "Dancing with the Stars: The Next Pro" on its debut season.

Known for her meticulous eye, Shirley Ballas earned the nickname "Queen of Latin" during her time as a record-breaking competitive dancer. She is also mother of pro Mark Ballas , who is paired with reality star Maura Higgins on Season 35. And she didn't hold back when it came to her judging, handing out scores as low as 4.

The night also marked the return of pro Val Chmerkovskiy , who was absent last week after being suspended for making a controversial social media remark that appeared to be a direct reference to Will Smith's Oscars slap at judge Carrie Ann Inaba . He and Inaba shared a heartfelt moment, and the pro dancer also apologized to partner Jenna Dewan for creating "chaos" and pulling her into the mess.

Keep reading for a full recap of Horror Movie Night on "Dancing with the Stars."

'Dancing with the Stars' takes on 'Dedication Night' – Photos

Who got voted off 'DWTS' tonight? Double elimination takes two victims

10:01 PM ET, October 27 2026, Bryan Alexander

The Halloween Movie Night massacre on "Dancing with the Stars" claimed two couples on Oct. 27, as Jackson Olson and partner Emma Slater, along with Tyler Cameron and partner Sharna Burgess, were eliminated.

Tyler had appeared very upset after his dance. He apologized at the end, saying he was upset with his performance. Gave a classy goodbye to Burgess, his partner. Olson was all perky class in his farewell.

The double elimination followed last week's "Dedication Night," when all the contestants were spared elimination, setting up the brutal Halloween showdown.

The final three couples facing elimination were Olson and Slater, Cameron and Burgess, and Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik. Ali and Ravnik survived the scare.

The couples declared immediately safe were Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold, Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov, Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson, Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy, Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach, Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas, and Julia Stiles and Ezra Sosa.

Mark Ballas faces mom Shirley Ballas' judging with Maura Higgins

09:53 PM ET, October 27 2026, Joelle Goldstein

Rehearsal drama: Maura Higgins said she'd remember her dance from last week, which she dedicated to Ireland, for the rest of her life. But she'd be relishing in the happy moment even more with this week's challenge in front of her: dancing on Horror Movie Night with partner Mark Ballas' mom judging them. Not to mention, she had a Contemporary dance with a "lot of lifts with a lot of speed."

"I'm not an actress, people in the competition do this for a living so I just hope to God that I kill it," the "Traitors" alum said.

Dance: Higgins and Ballas danced to "Cry Little Sister (Theme from "the Lost Boys)" by Gerard McMann, inspired by "The Lost Boys." They nailed the creepy theme, with Higgins' blood-soaked gown, their fake fangs and white contacts.

Bruno Tonioli said she had a "fantastical lyrical quality" but urged her to extend her arms and really pull the movements from the floor. Derek Hough called Higgins a "phenomenal performer" and agreed that she needed to point her toes and extend the arms. Shirley Ballas called it "powerful" and said she'd like to see her feet rotate a bit more so that the routine will "flow" more.

And Carrie Ann Inaba panicked on the spot and forgot what she was going to say, only noting that she agreed with Tonioli. She later shouted out before giving her score that Higgins' "hands were gorgeous."

Amber Glenn spreads her wings with stunning 'Black Swan' tango

09:40 PM ET, October 27 2026, Bryan Alexander

Rehearsal drama: Olympic figure skater Amber Glenn was already a Season 35 favorite, but she pushed for even more with partner Pasha Pashkov. "We're at the top," Glenn said in the video. She was also taking on one of her favorite movies, "Black Swan," giving her extra motivation. "I can really relate to this movie," she said, talking about the pursuit of perfection and declaring, "I want to be the Black Swan." Glenn vowed to make "that 11-year-old me proud."

Dance: Glenn and Pashkov performed an Argentine Tango to "Perfection" by Clint Mansell, inspired by "Black Swan." Glenn fully embraced her dark transformation, sporting ghostly white makeup and a black feathered costume. The ballroom became a sinister ballet stage, filled with smoke and chandeliers, with feathers seemingly falling from the sky. Pashkov spun Glenn across the floor before the routine built to a high-kicking Tango climax, with Glenn dramatically whipping out her arm for the final flourish.

Shirley Ballas praised the "beautiful movement across the floor," adding, "I totally enjoyed it." Bruno Tonioli was so thrilled that he began flapping his arms like a swan, accidentally smacking Ballas in the process.

Carrie Ann Inaba called it "another wonderful performance," although she pointed out some tightness in Glenn's movements.

"You're exquisite to watch," Derek Hough told Glenn.

Tyler Cameron nearly walks off after low scores

09:31 PM ET, October 27 2026, Joelle Goldstein

Rehearsal drama: Tyler Cameron was coming off "the best night" of his life after revealing his fiancée was pregnant and they were having a baby girl. And with Halloween holding a special place in his heart after becoming a neighborhood favorite for handing out peanut butter, the Bachelor Nation star was determined not to go home.

"I don't wanna go home, I wanna work," he said. But it wouldn't be an easy feat, with partner Sharna Burgess demanding Cameron step up to the plate when it comes to his acting.

Dance: Cameron took the ballroom floor, appearing nearly unrecognizable with a long black-haired wig, top hat and fake facial hair. He and Burgess danced a passionate Viennese Waltz to "Love Song for a Vampire" by Annie Lennox, inspired by "Bram Stoker's Dracula," which ended with an intense chest stabbing.

However, the judges weren't totally moved by it. Derek Hough said it was "so smooth" but pointed out that his frame wasn't as strong as it needed to be. Shirley Ballas noted his "acting skills were great" but his technical skills needed work. Bruno Tonioli echoed that he "really felt it" with emotion, but he lost his frame.

Carrie Ann Inaba tested the waters, saying she disagreed with Ballas' feedback and that she didn't think the acting was very good and he "danced smaller" due to Burgess' shorter stature.

Score: 26/40, with Ballas giving a 5. Cameron was not happy by the scores, could barely muster a smile and tried to walk away from the camera shot before the show cut to commercial break. Yikes.

09:16 PM ET, October 27 2026, Bryan Alexander

Rehearsal drama: Jackson Olson was doing everything possible to escape the bottom of the "Dancing with the Stars" leaderboard, and embracing the Joker looked like his ticket out. But the iconic villain brought serious expectations. "There's a lot of pressure to live up to that," Olson said. He promised a startling transformation. "You're going to see this dark persona you don't see from me."

Dance: Olson and partner Emma Slater performed a contemporary to Frank Sinatra's "That's Life," inspired by "Joker." Both wore the villain's signature red suits, with Olson sporting toxic green hair. Against a Gotham City backdrop featuring an empty taxi and raging flames, Olson whipped Slater around his head in a series of wild lifts, even flashing a creepy little tongue wave during one manic move. He spun his partner into the finale as the set erupted in fake flames.

"You lit this place on fire!" declared co-host Alfonso Ribeiro. Carrie Ann Inaba called the performance "kind of weird in a good way."

"I hate clowns, but I loved that performance," Derek Hough said.

Guest judge Shirley Ballas called the routine "terrifying" and praised its challenging choreography. Bruno Tonioli declared, "The Joker is your trump card."

Score: 35/40. Three of Olson's first 9 scores and one Ballas 8.

Ezra Frech mom inspires Horror Movie Night before his painful leg injury

09:09 PM ET, October 27 2026, Joelle Goldstein

Rehearsal drama: Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach celebrated earning the first 10 of the season and were excited for the challenge ahead in Horror Movie Night, especially with Frech's close connection to the genre. After all, his mom, Bahar Soomekh, acted in "Saw III" though he wasn't particularly a fan of watching it. "No, I don't want to watch my mom get tortured on TV," he said.

The horror movie genre wasn't the only scare happening this week. Frech also suffered a blister injury near where his prosthetic leg connected to his limb. He said felt like he was being "poked with a needle every step," but vowed to keep going. "I've put so much into this process so I'm just gonna fight through it," the Paralympian said.

Dance: The duo danced a Jazz routine that was striking, haunting and powerful. There were tons of lifts and moments of Karagach throwing herself around the dance floor. You'd have no idea that Frech was battling such a painful injury. After the dance, Bruno Tonioli said he was like "a shape-shifting fiend," adding, "What a performance as always!"

Carrie Ann Inaba said she "couldn't tell" he was injured but encouraged him to focus more on his storytelling. Derek Hough commended his athleticism and how captivating he is to watch, but agreed on the storytelling feedback. Shirley Ballas, however, said she "enjoyed the storyline" and lifts.

Connor Wood brings creepy Annabelle doll to life in freaky contemporary

08:56 PM ET, October 27 2026, Bryan Alexander

Rehearsal drama: Connor Wood was still riding high after last week's strong performance but knew he needed to escape the bottom two. Wood and partner Rylee Arnold took on a contemporary dance inspired by the horror film "Annabelle: Creation," with Arnold playing the demonic doll and Wood portraying her toymaker.

Dance: Wood and Arnold performed to "You Are My Sunshine" by Charles McDonald. The creepy routine opened with Wood bringing his lifeless partner to life on a couch. Arnold was a freaky Annabelle on the ballroom floor, with Wood keeping up as he tossed her around like a rag doll and even executed a somersault on the couch. The impressively creepy performance drew thunderous applause.

Guest judge Shirley Ballas called the dance "outstanding" and said she would be having nightmares. Bruno Tonioli declared, "You killed the routine," adding, "It was like watching a mini-movie."

Carrie Ann Inaba went even further. "I crown you the Contemporary King," she proclaimed. "You disappeared into that dance."

Scores: 37/40, with Carrie Ann and Derek giving 10s.

Val Chmerkovskiy returns to the ballroom, gets compliment from Carrie Ann Inaba

08:49 PM ET, October 27 2026, Joelle Goldstein

Rehearsal drama: Val Chmerkovskiy celebrated reuniting with his partner Jenna Dewan after his one-week suspension, telling her, "I am so sorry for all the chaos, you did not sign up for that and I feel awful." She accepted his apology and offered a hug, before focusing their sights on the Argentine Tango inspired by "Zombie" movies this week. "We're pushing the envelope with lifts," Chmerkovskiy said.

But it wouldn't be an easy task, since Dewan said she had a genetic upper back issue that would pose some issues. Still, she was determined to get past it. "I'm fighting through," she told cameras.

Dance: Simply stated, the dance was powerful, it was full of passion, they had precision on the footwork, and impressed with the lifts. It delivered all the goods. And the judges said as much, with Derek Hough calling it "one of the best Argentine Tangos I've ever seen on this floor."

Shirley Ballas commended Dewan for properly "twisting" the upper and lower halves of her body. She pointed out there was a "little hiccup" in the routine when Dewan's foot got stuck in her dress, but she kicked it off and kept going like a pro. Bruno Tonioli also celebrated the "power and passion" of the dance.

But it was Carrie Ann Inaba who raised eyebrows with her feedback, giving Chmerkovskiy a compliment right off the bat. "Incredible choreography, Val," she said. She also told the pair, "The dance as a whole was perfection." Looks like all the drama is behind us!

Tatyana Ali bares her fangs in bloody 'Sinners' paso doble

08:35 PM ET, October 27 2026, Bryan Alexander

Rehearsal drama: Tatyana Ali was still riding high from last week's performance but was determined to survive Halloween Night, especially with Latin dance expert Shirley Ballas serving as a guest judge. Rehearsals were brutal, with Ali taking several tumbles. But she defiantly vowed to "survive."

Dance: Ali and partner Jan Ravnik performed a Paso Doble to "I Lied to You" by Miles Caton, inspired by "Sinners." Whipping a white dress on the floor, Ali was a fierce presence, even ripping a piece of Ravnik's cheek skin off in a gruesome special effect. The vampire-themed dance ended with Ali baring her fangs over her partner.

Carrie Ann Inaba called it Ali's "most powerful dance yet," although she felt the flowing skirt occasionally overpowered her movements. Derek Hough was sold. "Whatever you're selling, I'm buying," he said, calling the performance "epic."

But Ballas wasn't biting. The Latin expert complained that the routine "had no recognizable Paso Doble." She added, "As a Paso Doble goes, it didn't do it for me."

Bruno Tonioli dubbed Ballas the "queen of meanness" before praising Ali's performance.

Score: 28/40, with Shirley giving another 4! Ouch.

Harry Shum Jr., Jenna Johnson 'saw' their way to a perfect score

08:30 PM ET, October 27 2026, Joelle Goldstein

Rehearsal drama: Harry Shum Jr. said he doesn't "particularly like being scared" so this week's Horror Movie Night was not really his thing. "I'm not pretending to be tortured and die," he said. However, partner Jenna Johnson was excited because they had a contemporary dance, which meant they'd be diving into "some tricks and lifts" − likely a thrill for her after being scolded by Carrie Ann Inaba for lifts two weeks ago.

Dance: The "Glee" star danced a terrifying "Saw"-inspired contemporary with a surprise ending cameo from the film's Jigsaw Killer on a bicycle. He contorted his body, pulled off some impressive lifts and tricks, and effectively scared the whole ballroom.

Following the dance, Bruno Tonioli said he "could taste the fear," calling the routine "perfection." Carrie Ann Inaba stood up and simply said, "Bravo." She also praised the dance as "so perfect, so dynamic." (Quite the redemption for these two after the lift drama!) Derek Hough commended the partnership between Shum Jr. and Johnson, as well as the way Shum Jr. committed to the routine.

Tough cookie Shirley Ballas was equally as impressed, saying she "loved your locomotive movements" and that she had "never seen anything quite like that." (Definitely a change-up from her last score!)

Score: 40/40, marking the first perfect score of the season.

Julia Stiles gets freaky in 'The Omen' but DWTS' Shirley Ballas is so unimpressed

08:14 PM ET, October 27 2026, Bryan Alexander

Rehearsal drama: Julia Stiles was still emotional over the outpouring of support for last week's tribute to her "10 Things I Hate About You" co-star Heath Ledger. But the actress, who appeared in the 2006 remake of "The Omen," was ready to get sinister. Rehearsals weren't easy. "Can I just remind everybody I'm 45 years old?" Stiles said. She also warned partner Ezra Sosa about his moods. "You're a cranky bitch when you're tired," she told him.

Dance: Stiles and Sosa performed an Argentine Tango to "The Dogs Attack" by Jerry Goldsmith, Lionel Newman and the National Philharmonic Orchestra, inspired by "The Omen." Wearing a red dress and black heels, Stiles got downright freaky in a church setting, surrounded by veiled women in red dresses. Sosa was the sexy priest who could dance. Stiles even had blood-red beads streaming from each eyes like blood.

Guest host Shirley Ballas was downright harsh in her first critique, hitting on Stiles' form. She's so harsh that the camera caught one of Stiles' family members sticking out her tongue at Shirley from the audience.

"I didn't know you could do that to a priest," joked Bruno Tonioli, calling Ballas, "The mistress of evil." Carrie Ann Inaba found the performance "tense and stiff" and wanted to see Stiles loosen up. Derek Hough suggested the dance "might have been a little hiccup in the journey."

Scores: 26/40 with Shirley giving a dismal 4. Shirley sent an instant message and Stiles was stunned. Nobody gives 4's on "DWTS." Certainly not to Julia Stiles.

08:09 PM ET, October 27 2026, Joelle Goldstein

It's time to get spooky on "Dancing with the Stars." A "Saw"-themed pre-taped package opened the show before guest judge Shirley Ballas made her way into the ballroom − and she wasted no time in bringing the scares.

"Neglect the technique at your own peril," she warned the contestants, or face the consequences of getting a 2.

Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough also reminded viewers of the night's big twist: a double elimination. Heading into the night, Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov had the advantage, sitting at the top of the leaderboard with 38/40. Meanwhile, three couples tied at the bottom with 32/40: Jackson Olson and Emma Slater, Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik, and Tyler Cameron and Sharna Burgess.

'DWTS' voting: How to vote online for Season 35 cast

07:15 PM ET, October 27 2026, Liza Esquibias

Voting opens when the show begins at 8 p.m. ET and closes after the last competitive dance of the evening. Fans can vote up to ten times per couple either online on ABC's website, or by texting the celebrity's first name to "21523" (standard text rates apply).

At the end of the night, the celebrity with combined lowest number of votes and judges' scores will be eliminated from the competition. However, this week will feature a spooky twist, with two couples being sent home at the end of the night.

What were the scores on 'DWTS' last week?

07:00 PM ET, October 27 2026, Liza Esquibias

Week 6 of the competition was Dedication Night , where the celebrity contestants honored the people and places that hold a special place in their hearts. The night ended with no elimination – and a very excited group of 10 remaining couples. The scores of the night are below.

Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach: 37 out of 40

Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik: 32 out of 40

Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas: 35 out of 40

Jackson Olson and Emma Slater: 32 out of 40

Julia Stiles honors Heath Ledger with 'Dancing with the Stars' tribute — Photos

Before 'Dancing with the Stars' Halloween night: Recapping Season 35 so far

06:30 PM ET, October 27 2026, Liza Esquibias

"Dancing with the Stars" Season 35 kicked off with a two-night premiere, featuring performances by the male celebrities on Tuesday, Sept. 15, followed by the female celebrities on Wednesday, Sept. 16. Each danced to a No. 1 song from the year they were born. Week 1 ended with the double elimination of Connor Leavitt and Adele Zaikman, who is a first-time pro after winning "Dancing with the Stars: Next Pro," as well as Sarah Jane Nader and Hailey Bills, also a first-time pro.

Week 2 was Viral Hits Night , which marked the first time this season that all the contestants came together. Each couple danced to catchy tunes that have gone viral on social media, and Giada De Laurentiis and Alan Bersten were sent home at the end of the evening.

Week 3 had a Yacht Rock theme, featuring a lineup of "smooth grooves, soft-rock classics and iconic hits that defined" the iconic era. The episode ultimately saw in the elimination of Taylor Hanson and Britt Stewart.

For Week 4 of the competition , the routines paid tribute to Mariah Carey and her iconic discography. Ciara Miller and Brandon Armstrong were voted off.

Super Bowl Night was Week 5, where the couples paid tribute to the performers who have headlined a Super Bowl halftime show. It ended with fan favorites Guillermo Rodriguez and Witney Carson being sent home.

Week 6 marked Dedication Night , honoring the people and places that hold a special place in the hearts of the celebrity contestants. Each performance brought tears to the ballroom – including Julia Stiles' "10 Things I Hate About You" costars coming out to remember the late Heath Ledger , and Tyler Cameron and his fiancée Tate Madden announcing their pregnancy before learning that they are having a baby girl live on air. There was no elimination last week.

Val Chmerkovskiy 'Dancing with the Stars' suspension lifted, pro returns to ballroom

06:00 PM ET, October 27 2026, Liza Esquibias

Last week, Val Chmerkovskiy became the first pro in "Dancing with the Stars" history to not be allowed to dance with his celebrity partner, Jenna Dewan , for an episode. This was due to his suspension from the show for a social media post he made implying he wanted to slap judge Carrie Ann Inaba like Will Smith did to Chris Rock , after he made a joke about the actor's wife Jada Pinkett Smith, at the 2022 Oscars.

"You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night," Chmerkovskiy wrote, referring to Smith's character on "The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air." The post was seemingly in response to a critique Inaba gave Chmerkovskiy's wife Jenna Johnson, also a pro, and her partner Harry Shum Jr., for doing a controversial lift during their Oct. 13 performance.

He later apologized, writing on Oct. 15, "I should have never made the reference that I did and I deeply regret it." On Oct. 17, however, BBC Studios revealed Chmerkovskiy – who has been a "DWTS" pro since Season 13 in 2011 – would not be participating in Week 6 of the competition.

Chmerkovskiy, 40, apologized again in a statement, writing, "In a moment where my instinct was to defend my wife, I made a poor decision to reference a meme to 'keep my wife's name' out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention."

Inaba broke her silence on the situation in an Oct. 25 Instagram comment: "I have not spoke about what happened because of professional courtesy for those who are still competing, and we actually have standards and practices that keep us separated. But I think a part of this 'headline' has missed a few important parts of what happened.

"I think it's important for everyone to know that Jenna and I hugged it out after the Super Bowl show. Jenna was an absolute professional about it, and two women worked through the moment. It came to my attention later that Jenna was deeply hurt. So I also offered to speak with her at anytime. I have also offered to discuss the lift rule and how I enforce it. @sharnaburgess made a great video explaining lifts, assists and which dances allow and don't allow them," she said.

Alan Bersten took Chmerkovskiy's place for Dedication Night, with him and Dewan, 45, performing a Viennese Waltz to "Unchained Melody" by The Righteous Brothers in honor of her mom. The routine earned "The Rookie" star her first 10 of the season, which came from Inaba.

The suspension was only briefly addressed at the beginning of the episode, when cohost Alfonso Ribeiro simply said that "Val is not with us this week" and explained that Week 3 eliminee Bersten would be subbing in.

Chmerkovskiy will be back tonight, according to the series' official Instagram page. In an Oct. 25 Story post, Dewan said, "Hi, everybody. Here we are. We are here for 'Halloween Horror Movie Night.' We are doing an Argentine tango to the song 'Uninvited,' inspired by the movie '28 Weeks Later.'"

'Dancing with the Stars' theme this week: Horror Movie Night songs and dances

05:45 PM ET, October 27 2026, Liza Esquibias

Horror Movie Night celebrates the upcoming Halloween holiday, with "thrills, chills and killer choreography" in the 10 remaining couples' dances inspired by legendary horror films. Here are the dances and songs that each couple will be dancing to.

Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik: Paso Doble to "I Lied to You" by Miles Caton, inspired by "Sinners"

Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy: Argentine Tango to "Uninvited" by Damned Anthem and Kendra Dantes, inspired by "Zombie" movies

Jackson Olson and Emma Slater: Contemporary to "That's Life" by Frank Sinatra, inspired by "Joker"

Amber Glenn and partner Pasha Pashkov: Argentine Tango to "Perfection" by Clint Mansell, inspired by "Black Swan"

Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold: Contemporary to "You Are My Sunshine" by Charles McDonald, inspired by "Annabelle: Creation"

Tyler Cameron and Sharna Burgess: Viennese Waltz to "Love Song for a Vampire" by Annie Lennox, inspired by "Bram Stoker's Dracula"

Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas: Contemporary to "Cry Little Sister (Theme from "the Lost Boys)" by Gerard McMann, inspired by "The Lost Boys"

Julia Stiles and Ezra Sosa: Argentine Tango to "The Dogs Attack" by Jerry Goldsmith, Lionel Newman and National Philharmonic Orchestra, inspired by "The Omen"

05:31 PM ET, October 27 2026, Liza Esquibias

"Dancing with the Stars" airs live on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+. The episode can be streamed the next day on Hulu and Disney+.

articles.title: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
articles.summary: “Crackgate” reports of broken iPhone Duo screens may be due to an issue where a part of the hinge pushes up against the inside screen.
articles.body: Within hours of the iPhone Duo launch last Friday, people reported that the inner screen on some brand new foldable phones was already broken. The issue was similar across many photos shared on social media: some kind of issue or crack would appear in the middle of the screen above the hinge, with lines appearing on the right side of the display. On Monday, Apple acknowledged an “issue” and said it’s replacing damaged units, without going into much detail about how many broken phones have been reported so far. So what’s actually going on? Shahram Mokhtari, the lead teardown technician at iFixit, has actually taken apart the iPhone Duo and has a pretty good idea about the potential cause, telling The Verge that it’s due to an issue along the hinge, where a series of gears, springs, and joints work together to let the device close flat, while also trying to avoid creating a deeper crease by giving that screen space to bend more gently inside while it’s closed. [Image: The iPhone Duo’s hinge. At the troublesome spot, it appears that the flexible inner screen is pushing up against a part of the hinge. That inner screen is already “extremely sensitive,” he says — if you took a pick or a sharp tool and poked at the edges of the screen, “you’re going to break that screen.” If you look at the pictures of damaged Duos on social media, there’s often a black spot where the damage is focused on the display, and that’s where the metal is hitting the screen, Mokhtari says. [Image: You can see a visual representation of what Mokhtari is talking about in iFixit’s written and video Duo teardowns, which reveal where the hinge transitions, as the center hinge support makes space for a crossing flex cable, creating several edges that could ultimately be the culprit. The damage iFixit has been seeing is at a point where the center support bar might not always drop down far enough while the screen folds, possibly creating a stress “hot spot” between the flat bar and the bent screen inside a closed iPhone Duo. [Media: At least one user with a broken Duo screen said they “felt something around the internal hinge” while showing it to a friend, kept opening it, and heard an “audible crack,” with the screen breaking. YouTuber CuriousHagi, who covered a Duo with dirt as part of a strenuous durability test, captured something similar on video, and the screen break appears in a similar spot. In a teardown video, CuriousHagi found that a part of the hinge that connects to the central bar had snapped. [Media: Apple says the issue affects a “small number” of Duo units, and Mokhtari says that “In terms of numbers, we don’t know. Apple definitely has all the data here. And I suspect they know more than they’re telling us as well.” But he notes that because foldable screens are so delicate, a “certain number” of them will fail, as will a number of the hinges because they’re also “extremely complicated and delicate.” And while Apple isn’t recalling the Duos, “If three months from now, we’re still seeing the same kind of failure, then it’s a more widespread problem, and that might lead to a recall,” Mokhtari says. Mokhtari points out that since this is the first generation of the iPhone Duo, it’s the first time Apple’s engineers are getting data on the hinge, and he says that “I guarantee you” Apple will redesign what’s at fault here for its next-generation foldable. He also notes that, generally speaking, “the phones do seem to be in people’s hands and people are using them, and they’re not running into any issues whatsoever.”

articles.title: Amazon debuts the Alexa Photo Frame and Echo Time smart clock, plus other upgraded devices | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon's other new devices include an upgraded Echo Dot, an Echo Studio with visual intelligence features, and the Echo Show 16.
articles.body:
Amazon unveiled five new Alexa devices today, including two new kinds of hardware: the Alexa Photo Frame , a smart picture frame, and the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock.

The Alexa Photo Frame is Amazon’s foray into the world of digital photo displays, a product category that has transcended from a clunky, last-minute holiday gift to a sleek, attractive way to look through your camera roll.

Aura is responsible for much of the growth in this category, so it’s no coincidence that the Alexa Photo Frame has a similar aesthetic feel: The screen is much easier on the eyes than the old, bright photo frames from years past. The device is said to be specifically calibrated for sharing photos, featuring a semi-matte, anti-glare display that makes it look more like a Samsung Frame TV than a laptop screen.

Also like Aura, the Photo Frame’s 10-inch screen looks like a matte photograph, helping it blend in with other artwork on your wall.

Amazon’s new device, though, adds the value of integration with users’ existing Amazon accounts. Prime members get unlimited storage on Amazon Photos, and Alexa+ is supposed to intelligently choose how and when to display photos.

“It knows to choose photos where you’re smiling and the lighting is right, and it matches the season you’re in, so you see last year’s family Halloween costumes in October instead of the middle of spring. It also knows what to skip, like screenshots and receipts,” Amazon said in a press release. You can also add voice notes to photos, and images sync automatically as you take them.

The Alexa Photo Frame is on sale now , and starts at $199.99 in Black, and $229 in Birch or Walnut wood.

Meanwhile, the Echo Time clock seems to be a response to the growing sentiment that people don’t want to rely on their phones for alarms, setting morning reminders, or checking the weather.

“Millions of customers start and end their days with Alexa — checking the weather and turning on the lights from bed in the morning or winding down with white noise at night,” Amazon wrote. “But the bedroom asks for something different from a device than the kitchen or living room does — so we designed an Echo specifically for it.”

Amazon says that the Echo Time , which costs $199.99, or $209.99 for a Kids version, has opt-in sleep sensing tools. You can choose to set a smart alarm feature that wakes you up within a 10 to 60 minute window of your alarm time, and can wake you when it detects you’re in a lighter phase of sleep, so that it’s less jarring to begin your day.

Like the popular Hatch alarm clocks, the clock can also mimic sunrise features to ease you awake.

Amazon also showed off updates to its existing lines of devices. We now get the Echo Show 16, a new Echo Dot, and Echo Studio with Home Camera.

The biggest upgrade to the Echo Dot is that it now includes a built-in smart home hub, which also includes an eero Wi-Fi extender that adds up to 1,000 square feet of coverage, helping it connect to lights, locks, and thermostats around your home. The new Echo Dot is also powered by Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon chip, which is said to make it better at on-device processing to speed up conversations with its AI, Alexa+.

Amazon says its most advanced speaker, however, is the Echo Studio with Home Camera. This speaker doubles as a camera so you can check on your home while you’re out, and also has visual intelligence features.

“Alexa can also see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help you in real time,” Amazon explained. “Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa+ to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.”

The Echo Dot is available at $99.99, and the Echo Studio with Home Camera costs $249.99.

Finally, Amazon unveiled the new Echo Show 16, which includes a 16-inch display. Amazon says the device has a 10% larger viewing area than its predecessor, but with a 40% smaller frame. It has Fire TV built in, plus Smart Home tools like Family Organizer. It can also function like a digital photo frame.

The Echo Show 16 is available for preorder for $499.99.

articles.title: Apple raises the MacBook Neo’s student pricing again
articles.summary: Apple increased the MacBook Neo’s Education Store starting price to $649, a price hike of $150 compared to its initial education pricing.
articles.body: The MacBook Neo now starts at $649 on Apple’s Education Store, up $150 from its initial $499 education starting price. As reported earlier by MacRumors, the student discount for the Neo received a $50 price bump in recent days, following a $100 price bump back in June. Apple’s budget MacBook is now just $50 off its regular $699 starting price for students, rather than the usual $100 discount. The now-$649 starting configuration includes 256GB of storage and 8GB of RAM, and doesn’t include Touch ID. The MacBook Neo’s starting price was its biggest selling point when it launched in March, but that perk has been steadily eroding, largely due to shortages of RAM and other components. In June, Apple raised the Neo’s regular starting price to $699 and its Education Store starting price to $599. It also hiked prices for iPads, another student favorite, at the same time, along with most of its other products. There are rumors Apple has another MacBook Neo in the works, potentially with more RAM, that could launch early next year.
